elements.name: Parent User
elements.rationale: Role-check facts across backend and frontend show the system explicitly recognizes and authorizes a parent role interacting with multiple services.

elements.name: Child User
elements.rationale: Role-check facts show the application distinguishes a child role and presents/permits child-specific interactions.

elements.name: Administrator
elements.rationale: Admin-only role checks indicate a separate external actor with privileged user-management access.

elements.name: Authentication Service
elements.rationale: The auth router is mounted as one backend service and implements registration, multiple login flows, current-user lookup, and password change with database reads/writes.

elements.name: Child Profile Service
elements.rationale: The children router is mounted as one coherent service handling child profile CRUD, approvals, and history-related operations against child and video data.

elements.name: Video Service
elements.rationale: The videos router is mounted as a single service providing upload, browse, detail, stream, update, delete, like, and comment behavior with video datastore operations.

elements.name: User Profile and Administration Service
elements.rationale: The users router is mounted as one service for profile retrieval/update, stats, user listing, role change, and deletion operations.

elements.name: Image Upload Handler
elements.rationale: Multer-based image upload middleware is reused by registration and child-profile routes and writes uploaded images to server filesystem storage.

elements.name: Video Upload and Streaming Handler
elements.rationale: Video-related upload middleware writes files to server storage and the videos router also exposes a streaming endpoint, forming a coherent media file handling process.
elements.uncertainty_note: The facts clearly show upload storage and a stream route, but do not explicitly show filesystem reads for streaming; grouping upload and streaming is a reasonable analyst abstraction.

elements.name: User Accounts Database
elements.rationale: Mongoose model/collection facts and multiple user read/write operations show persistent storage of user account records in the users collection.

elements.name: Child Profiles Database
elements.rationale: The ChildProfile model maps to a persistent MongoDB collection and is heavily read and updated by child-profile related routes.

elements.name: Video Metadata Database
elements.rationale: The Video model maps to the videos collection and route facts show persistent reads, writes, aggregates, and populate operations over stored video records.

elements.name: Uploaded Image Files
elements.rationale: Filesystem location and write facts show uploaded images stored under the backend uploads area, which is also statically exposed by the server.

elements.name: Uploaded Video Files
elements.rationale: Filesystem storage facts show uploaded media files written under the backend uploads area and exposed through a static mount.
elements.uncertainty_note: The facts show a shared uploads directory for static serving and a video upload subflow, but they do not explicitly partition files by media type beyond the separate upload middleware paths.

elements.name: Browser Local Storage
elements.rationale: Frontend web storage access facts show persistent browser-side storage of token, user, and cookie-banner state in localStorage.
